div.head: What is marked in the text
div.p: Inside the body, only the elements of the annotation layers appear: names of persons, places and events; works named; statements with their reference and quotation; formulas; dates; notes of three types (sources, parallels, editorial remarks); scribal changes; what is unclear or missing; page and line breaks; other languages; and editorial corrections. For the rare doubtful cases, an editor's addition is supplied, and an abbreviation with its expansion a choice of abbr and expan. A record of a kind no name element fits is rs, its kind in type and its record in ref, in the names' forms; a point that a stand-off annotation refers to is an anchor. A span that crosses others or the structure, such as a quotation over several paragraphs, is split into fragments, each nesting where it stands, joined by next and prev, which point to each other.

A quotation and a note point to their sources in source, in one of these forms: a document's code (C.NIC-0325), alone or with a citation after an underscore (C.NIC-0325_3, COLL.Dach.ms-Brn-Burg-425_2.49); a Bible reference, by one code per book, chapter and verse (MAT_18_19, PHP_3_17-20); a work by its Gryson siglum, with the place cited (IS_ety_1.2.3); or an SCTA resource. A loose reference starts with cf_. Names point to their records by placeholders (#new_person_…) until the import resolves them, then by permalinks.

A gap may say why the text is missing, in reason: lacuna (the witness lacks it: lost leaves, or a lacuna in the edition it comes from), damage, illegible (unclear is for what can be half read), reproduction (not readable in the images or the film used), deleted (struck out and not readable), sampling (not transcribed, by the encoder's choice: an incipit and an explicit only) or editorial (left out for another reason, given in a note); without a reason, it's unknown. Its extent, where known, is a quantity with its unit (leaves, lines, words, chars), or extent in words.

constraintSpec.desc: In the text, a note's type is its layer.

sch:rule.sch:assert: A note in the text is typed source, parallel or editorial.

constraintSpec.desc: A note holds words, or its codes in source.

sch:rule.sch:assert: A note holds words, or its codes in @source.

constraintSpec.desc: A source note's codes are in source, not in its words.

valItem.desc: in the text: the source a passage comes from, its codes in source
in the text: a parallel elsewhere ("Cf. concil. Mogunt. 847 c. 3")
in the text: an editor's remark
in a record: the links to the record in other catalogues
in a record: the authority files that describe it
in a bibliographic record: what fits nowhere else

attDef.desc: the sources the note points to: see the pointers' forms

dataSpec.desc: A pointer to a source: a document's code, alone or with a citation after an underscore (C.NIC-0325_3); a Bible reference by book, chapter and verse (MAT_18_19, PHP_3_17-20); a Gryson siglum and the place cited (IS_ety_1.2.3); each may start with cf_ for a loose reference; or an SCTA resource. A code holds letters, digits, dots and hyphens; an underscore only separates a code from its citation.

constraintSpec.desc: A fragment's @next points to the next fragment in the file, of the same kind, whose @prev points back.

sch:assert.test: count($next) = 1 and local-name($next) = local-name() and normalize-space($next/@prev) = concat('#', @xml:id)

sch:rule.sch:assert: <>'s @next () points to the next fragment in the file, a <> whose @prev points back.

constraintSpec.desc: A fragment's @prev points to the previous fragment in the file, of the same kind, whose @next points back.

sch:assert.test: count($prev) = 1 and local-name($prev) = local-name() and normalize-space($prev/@next) = concat('#', @xml:id)

sch:rule.sch:assert: <>'s @prev () points to the previous fragment in the file, a <> whose @next points back.

attDef.desc: the source quoted: see the pointers' forms

valItem.desc: a formula introducing an authority ("ut lex dicit")
a statement's reference whose claim sits in a heading

dataSpec.desc: A pointer to a record: a placeholder (#new_person_…), an identifier in the file, or a permalink.
